readings.subsection: The Judgment of Tyre and Sidon
readings.title: The Coastlands Tremble at Tyre's Fall
readings.subtitle: The Princes of the Sea Lament
readings.text: [Ezekiel 26:15] “Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to Tsor, <dq>‘Would the coastlands not shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded cry, when the killing occurs in your midst?</dq> [16] <dq>And all the princes of the sea shall come down from their thrones, and they shall lay aside <dn>את</dn> their robes, and take off <dn>את</dn> their embroidered garments, and put on trembling, and sit on the ground. And they shall tremble continuously, and they shall be astonished at you.</dq> [17] <dq>And they shall take up <dn>את</dn> a lamentation for you, and say to you, “How you have perished, O one inhabited by seafaring men, the city well-praised, who was strong at sea, she and her inhabitants, who put their fear on all her inhabitants!</dq> [18] <dq>Now the coastlands tremble on the day of your fall! And the coastlands by the sea shall shudder at your going out.” ’</dq> [19] <dq>“For thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘When <dn>I</dn> make you a ruined city, like cities no longer inhabited, when <dn>I</dn> bring <dn>את</dn> the deep upon you, and great waters cover you,</dq> [20] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall bring you down with <dn>את</dn> those who go down into the pit, to the people of old. And <dn>I</dn> shall make you dwell in the lowest part of the earth, in wastes of old, with those who go to the pit, so that you do not return. But <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> splendour in the land of the living.</dq> [21] <dq><dn>I</dn> make you a horror, and let you be no more. And you are sought for, but never found again,’ declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Judgment of Tyre and Sidon
readings.title: A Lamentation for Tyre
readings.subtitle: The Magnificent Ship of State
readings.text: [Ezekiel 27:1] The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came again to me, saying, [2] “Now, son of man, take up <dn>את</dn> a lamentation for Tsor, [3] and you shall say to Tsor, ‘You who dwell at the entrance to the sea, merchant of the peoples on many coastlands, thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“O Tsor, you yourself have said, ‘<dn>I</dn> am perfect in loveliness.’</dq> [4] <dq>“Your borders are in the heart of the seas. Your builders have perfected your loveliness.</dq> [5] <dq>“They have made all your timbers of fir trees from Senir. They took <dn>את</dn> a cedar from Leḇanon to make a mast for you.</dq> [6] <dq>“From the oaks of Bashan they made your oars. They made your deck with ivory from the coasts of Kittim.</dq> [7] <dq>“Of fine embroidered linen from Mitsrayim was your sail to serve you as banner. Of blue and purple from the coasts of Elishah was your covering.</dq> [8] <dq>“The inhabitants of Tsiḏon and Arvaḏ were your seamen. Your wise men, O Tsor, were in you, they were your sailors.</dq> [9] <dq>“The elders of Geḇal and its wise men were in you repairing your seams. All the ships of the sea and their seamen were in you to trade your merchandise.</dq> [10] <dq>“Those from Persia, Luḏ, and Put were in your army as men of battle. Shield and helmet they hung up within you, they gave <dn>את</dn> splendour to you.</dq> [11] <dq>“The sons of Arvaḏ, and your army were on your walls all around, and the Gammaḏites were in your towers. They hung their shields on your walls all around, they perfected <dn>את</dn> your loveliness.</dq>

readings.subsection: The Judgment of Tyre and Sidon
readings.title: Tyre's Extensive Commerce
readings.subtitle: A Catalogue of Trading Partners
readings.text: [Ezekiel 27:12] <dq>“Tarshish was your merchant because of your great wealth. They gave you silver, iron, tin, and lead for your merchandise.</dq> [13] <dq>“Yavan, Tuḇal, and Mesheḵ were your traders. They exchanged <dn>את</dn> slaves and <dn>את</dn> objects of bronze for your merchandise.</dq> [14] <dq>“Those from the house of Toḡarmah exchanged horses, and horsemen, and mules for your merchandise.</dq> [15] <dq>“The men of Deḏan traded with you. Many isles were your market, they brought you ivory tusks and ebony as payment.</dq> [16] <dq>“Aram was your merchant because of the multitude of your works. They gave you emeralds, purple, and embroidery, and fine linen, and corals, and rubies for your wares.</dq> [17] <dq>“Yehuḏah and the land of Yisra’ěl were your traders. For your merchandise they exchanged <dn>את</dn> wheat of Minnith, and <dn>את</dn> early figs, and <dn>את</dn> honey, and <dn>את</dn> oil, and <dn>את</dn> balm.</dq> [18] <dq>“Dammeseq was your merchant because of the multitude of your works, because of your great wealth of goods, with the wine of Ḥelbon and with white wool.</dq> [19] <dq>“Weḏan and Yavan from Uzal paid for your wares, they exchanged <dn>את</dn> wrought iron, <dn>את</dn> cassia, and <dn>את</dn> cane for your merchandise.</dq> [20] <dq>“Deḏan traded with you in saddlecloths for riding.</dq> [21] <dq>“Araḇia, and all princes of Qěḏar, were merchants for you. In lambs, and rams, and goats they were your merchants.</dq> [22] <dq>“The traders of Sheḇa and Ra‛mah were your traders. They paid for your wares with the choicest spices, and all kinds of precious stones, and gold.</dq> [23] <dq>"Ḥaran, and Kanneh, and Ěḏen, traders of Sheḇa, Ashshur, and Kilmaḏ traded with you.</dq> [24] <dq>“They traded with you in perfect items, in purple clothes, in embroidered garments, in chests of multi-coloured clothes, in strong twined cords, among your merchandise.</dq> [25] <dq>“The ships of Tarshish were the travellers of your merchandise. And you were filled and richly laden in the heart of the seas.</dq>

readings.subsection: The Judgment of Tyre and Sidon
readings.title: The Shipwreck of Tyre
readings.subtitle: The Nations Mourn Her Downfall
readings.text: [Ezekiel 27:26] <dq>“Your seamen brought you into many waters, but the east wind broke you in the heart of the seas.</dq> [27] <dq>“Your wealth, and your wares, your merchandise, your mariners and your sailors, your repairers of seams, and your dealers in merchandise, and all your fighting men who are in you, and the entire company which is in your midst, shall go down into the heart of the seas on the day of your fall,</dq> [28] <dq>the coasts shaking at the sound of the cry of your sailors.</dq> [29] <dq>“And all the oarsmen, the mariners, all the sailors of the sea shall come down from their ships. They shall stand on the shore,</dq> [30] <dq>and they shall raise their voice and cry bitterly over you, and cast <dn>את</dn> dust on their heads, rolling themselves in ashes.</dq> [31] <dq>“And they shall shave themselves bald because of you, and shall gird themselves with sackcloth. And they shall weep for you with bitterness of heart and bitter wailing.</dq> [32] <dq>“And in their wailing for you they shall take up <dn>את</dn> a lamentation. And they shall lament for you, ‘Who is cut off in the midst of the sea like Tsor?</dq> [33] <dq>When your wares went out by sea, you have filled many peoples; with your great wealth and your merchandise you have made the sovereigns of the earth rich.</dq> [34] <dq>In the time you are broken by the seas in the depths of the waters, your merchandise and all your company shall fall in your midst.</dq> [35] <dq>All the inhabitants of the isles shall be astonished at you, and their sovereigns shall be greatly afraid, their faces shall be troubled.</dq> [36] <dq>The merchants among the peoples shall whistle at you. You shall become a horror, and be no more, forever.’ ” ’ ”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Judgment of Tyre and Sidon
readings.title: Prophecy Against the Prince of Tyre
readings.subtitle: Pride and Arrogance Judged
readings.text: [Ezekiel 28:1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [2] “Son of man, say to the prince of Tsor, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Because your heart is lifted up, and you say, ‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>Ěl</dn>, <dn>I</dn> sit in the seat of <dn>Elohim</dn>, in the heart of the seas,’ whereas you are a man, and not <dn>Ěl</dn>, though you set <dn>את</dn> your heart as the heart of <dn>Elohim</dn>!</dq> [3] <dq>“Look, are you wiser than Dani’ěl? Has no secret been hidden from you?</dq> [4] <dq>“By your wisdom and your understanding you have made riches for yourself, and gathered gold and silver into your treasuries.</dq> [5] <dq>“By your great wisdom, by your trade you have increased your riches, and your heart is lifted up because of your riches.”</dq> [6] <dq>Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Because you have set <dn>את</dn> your heart as the heart of <dn>Elohim</dn>,</dq> [7] <dq>therefore see, <dn>I</dn> am bringing against you strangers, the ruthless ones of the nations. And they shall draw their swords against the loveliness of your wisdom, and they shall profane <dn>את</dn> your splendour.</dq> [8] <dq>“Down into the pit they shall bring you, and you shall die the death of the slain in the heart of the seas.</dq> [9] <dq>“Would you still say before him who slays you, ‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>Elohim</dn>’, whereas you are man, and not <dn>Ěl</dn>, in the hand of him who kills you?</dq> [10] <dq>“The death of the uncircumcised you shall die, by the hand of foreigners. For <dn>I</dn> have spoken,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Judgment of Tyre and Sidon
readings.title: Lamentation for the King of Tyre
readings.subtitle: The Anointed Keruḇ Cast Down
readings.text: [Ezekiel 28:11] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [12] “Son of man, take up <dn>את</dn> a lamentation for the sovereign of Tsor, and you shall say to him, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“You were sealing up <dn>את</dn> a pattern, complete in wisdom and perfect in loveliness.</dq> [13] <dq>“You were in Ěḏen, the garden of <dn>Elohim</dn>. Every precious stone was <dn>את</dn> your covering: the ruby, topaz, and diamond, beryl, shoham, and jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emerald and gold. The workmanship of your settings and mountings was prepared for you on the day you were created.</dq> [14] <dq>“You were the anointed keruḇ that covered. And <dn>I</dn> placed you, you were on the set-apart mountain of <dn>Elohim</dn>. You walked up and down in the midst of stones of fire.</dq> [15] <dq>“You were perfect in your ways from the day you were created, until unrighteousness was found in you.</dq> [16] <dq>“By the greatness of your trade you became filled with violence within, and you sinned. So <dn>I</dn> thrust you from the mountain of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> destroyed you, O covering keruḇ, from the midst of the stones of fire.</dq> [17] <dq>“Your heart was lifted up because of your loveliness, you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendour. <dn>I</dn> threw you to the earth, <dn>I</dn> laid you before sovereigns, to look at you.</dq> [18] <dq>“You profaned <dn>את</dn> your set-apart places by your many crookednesses, by the unrighteousness of your trading. Therefore <dn>I</dn> brought forth <dn>את</dn> fire from your midst. It has devoured you, and <dn>I</dn> turned you to ashes upon the earth before the eyes of all who see you.</dq> [19] <dq>“All who knew you among the peoples were astonished at you. Waste you shall be, and cease to be, forever.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Judgment of Tyre and Sidon
readings.title: Prophecy Against Sidon
readings.subtitle: Judgment and Sanctification
readings.text: [Ezekiel 28:20] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [21] “Son of man, set <dn>את</dn> your face toward Tsiḏon, and prophesy against her, [22] and you shall say, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am against you, O Tsiḏon, and <dn>I</dn> shall be esteemed in your midst. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when <dn>I</dn> execute <dn>את</dn> judgments in her. And <dn>I</dn> shall be set-apart in her.</dq> [23] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall send <dn>את</dn> pestilence upon her, and <dn>את</dn> blood in her streets. And the slain shall fall in her midst by the sword against her, from all sides. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [24] <dq>“And there shall no longer be a pricking brier or a paining thorn for the house of Yisra’ěl from among all who are around them, who despise them. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Judgment of Tyre and Sidon
readings.title: Israel's Restoration Promised
readings.subtitle: Dwelling Safely in the Land
readings.text: [Ezekiel 28:25] Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“When <dn>I</dn> have gathered <dn>את</dn> the house of Yisra’ěl from the peoples among whom they are scattered, <dn>I</dn> shall be set-apart in them before the eyes of the nations. And they shall dwell in their own land which <dn>I</dn> gave to <dn>My</dn> servant Ya‛aqoḇ.</dq> [26] <dq>“And they shall dwell safely, and build houses, and plant vineyards, and dwell safely, when <dn>I</dn> execute <dn>את</dn> judgments on all those around them who despise them. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Siege and Destruction of Jerusalem
readings.title: The Fall of Jerusalem
readings.subtitle: King Zedekiah Captured and Judged
readings.text: [2 Kings 25:3] By the ninth of the new moon the scarcity of food had become so severe in the city that there was no food for the people of the land. [4] Then the city wall was breached, and all the men of battle fled at night by way of the gate between two walls, which was by the sovereign’s garden, even though the Kasdim were still encamped all around against the city. And the sovereign went by way of the desert plain. [5] And the army of the Kasdim pursued the sovereign, and overtook <dn>את</dn> him in the desert plains of Yeriḥo, and all his army was scattered from him. [6] And they seized <dn>את</dn> the sovereign and brought him up to the sovereign of Baḇel at Riblah, and they pronounced sentence on him. [7] And they slew <dn>את</dn> the sons of Tsiḏqiyahu before his eyes, and put out <dn>את</dn> the eyes of Tsiḏqiyahu, and bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Baḇel.

readings.subsection: The Siege and Destruction of Jerusalem
readings.title: Jerusalem Breached, The King Flees
readings.subtitle: The Fate of Zedekiah and His Sons
readings.text: [Jeremiah 52:6] On the ninth of the fourth new moon the scarcity of food was so severe in the city that there was no food for the people of the land. [7] Then the city wall was breached, and all the men of battle fled and went out of the city at night by way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the sovereign’s garden, while the Kasdim were near the city all around. And they went by way of the desert plain. [8] But the army of the Kasdim pursued the sovereign, and they overtook <dn>את</dn> Tsiḏqiyahu in the desert plains of Yeriḥo, and his entire army was scattered from him. [9] Then they captured <dn>את</dn> the sovereign and brought him up to the sovereign of Baḇel at Riḇlah in the land of Ḥamath, and he pronounced judgments on him. [10] And the sovereign of Baḇel slew <dn>את</dn> the sons of Tsiḏqiyahu before his eyes, and he also slew <dn>את</dn> all the heads of Yehuḏah in Riḇlah. [11] And he put out <dn>את</dn> the eyes of Tsiḏqiyahu. And the sovereign of Baḇel bound him in bronze shackles, and took him to Baḇel, and put him in prison till the day of his death.

readings.subsection: The Siege and Destruction of Jerusalem
readings.title: The City is Broken Into
readings.subtitle: The Remnant Exiled to Babylon
readings.text: [Jeremiah 39:2] In the eleventh year of Tsiḏqiyahu, in the fourth new moon, on the ninth day of the new moon, the city was broken into. [3] And all the heads of the sovereign of Baḇel came in and sat in the Middle Gate: Něrḡal-Shar’etser, Samgar-Neḇo, Sarseḵim, Raḇsaris, Něrḡal-Sarezer, Raḇmaḡ, and all the rest of the heads of the sovereign of Baḇel. [4] And it came to be, when Tsiḏqiyahu the sovereign of Yehuḏah and all the men of battle saw them, they fled and left the city by night, by way of the sovereign’s garden, by the gate between the two walls. And he went out toward the desert plain. [5] But the army of the Kasdim pursued them and overtook <dn>את</dn> Tsiḏqiyahu in the desert plains of Yeriḥo. And they captured him, and brought him up to Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sovereign of Baḇel, to Riḇlah in the land of Ḥamath, where he spoke judgment on him. [6] And the sovereign of Baḇel slew <dn>את</dn> the sons of Tsiḏqiyahu before his eyes in Riḇlah. The sovereign of Baḇel also slew <dn>את</dn> all the nobles of Yehuḏah. [7] And he put out <dn>את</dn> the eyes of Tsiḏqiyahu, and bound him with bronze shackles to bring him to Baḇel. [8] And the Kasdim burned <dn>את</dn> the house of the sovereign and <dn>את</dn> the houses of the people with fire, and they broke down <dn>את</dn> the walls of Yerushalayim. [9] And Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, exiled to Baḇel <dn>את</dn> the remnant of the people who remained in the city and those who defected to him, with the rest of the people who were left. [10] But Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, left in the land of Yehuḏah <dn>את</dn> the poor people, who had naught whatever, and gave them vineyards and fields on the same day.
